title: Measure a numeric mistake
summary: Absolute error is the size of the difference between an answer and a prediction. It drops the minus sign so the size is always nonnegative.
introduction: Absolute error is the size of the difference between an answer and a prediction. It drops the minus sign so the size is always nonnegative. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Absolute error is the size of the difference between an answer and a prediction. It drops the minus sign so the size is always nonnegative.

blocks.code:
answers = [4, 8]
predictions = [5, 6]
errors = [abs(a - p) for a, p in zip(answers, predictions)]
print(errors, sum(errors) / len(errors))
blocks.title: Measure a numeric mistake

blocks.text: The output is [1, 2] 1.5. The mistakes are one minute and two minutes. Their average is one and a half minutes.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the second prediction to 8 and find the new average error.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Keep the units: an error of 1.5 minutes is different from 1.5 hours.
For more detail later, use this [Machine Learning further reading](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course).
